name: BLANK BOARD: The Wordless Strategy
description: A purely analog two-player abstract strategy game played on an unmarked ceramic tile grid using unpainted river stones, with rules transmitted exclusively through oral tradition — no printed rulebook has ever been officially produced. The game's lack of any digital fingerprint makes it a quiet act of defiance in Shelf bars and Tier 2 back rooms, where players interpret moves through gesture and expression alone. Blank Board's rules mutate across neighborhoods, so a game in Ward Nine plays differently than the same stones placed in the Milwaukee Flats, generating fierce inter-district debates about what is 'correct.'
story_hooks: A specific sequence of moves — never written down — is rumored to be a pass-phrase used by an underground network, and someone at a Shelf bar just played it at the protagonist.
Two elderly women in a Milwaukee Flats bar have played daily for twenty years; one of them was a Tier 4 corporate archivist who disappeared from the official record in 2198.
A Spire anthropologist arrives to 'document' Blank Board for a cultural preservation grant — and the Shelf community must decide whether visibility is protection or a death sentence.
